skill.name: dast-ffuf
skill.description: Guides authorized ffuf dynamic application security testing for web content discovery, parameter fuzzing, virtual host enumeration, and result filtering.
skill.summary: Guides authorized ffuf-based DAST for web content, parameter, and virtual host fuzzing.
skill.author: AgentSecOps

security_audit.summary: I confirmed the remote pipe-to-shell CI installer and the intended active web-fuzzing workflows as security-relevant risks. Most static hits are false positives from Markdown code fences, placeholder URLs, security examples, and generic templates. No prompt injection attempt was found in the reviewed files.

remediation.issue: Remote installer executes network content in CI.
remediation.suggestion: Replace curl-to-bash with a pinned release, checksum verification, or a trusted action version.

remediation.issue: Authentication fuzzing can cause credential enumeration or account lockouts.
remediation.suggestion: Require written authorization, test accounts, low request rates, and explicit stop conditions before using these workflows.

remediation.issue: Active web fuzzing can affect unauthorized or production targets.
remediation.suggestion: Add a mandatory scope confirmation step with allowed hosts, rate limits, and excluded paths before scan planning.

remediation.issue: Generic template files create noisy security signals.
remediation.suggestion: Remove unused generic reference templates or tailor them to ffuf-specific safe usage guidance.

prompt_templates.title: Plan a safe content scan
prompt_templates.scenario: Beginner directory enumeration on an owned staging app
prompt_templates.prompt: Use dast-ffuf to plan an authorized directory scan for my staging app. Include scope, wordlist choice, filters, and rate limits.

prompt_templates.title: Fuzz API parameters
prompt_templates.scenario: Intermediate API testing after endpoints are known
prompt_templates.prompt: Create an ffuf plan to test approved API parameters. Include GET and POST cases, match rules, and validation steps.

prompt_templates.title: Review authentication testing scope
prompt_templates.scenario: Advanced login testing with strict authorization limits
prompt_templates.prompt: Design a controlled authentication fuzzing workflow for an approved test account. Include lockout safeguards and stop conditions.

prompt_templates.title: Design a CI DAST gate
prompt_templates.scenario: Advanced pipeline integration for a security team
prompt_templates.prompt: Draft a CI ffuf testing approach for staging. Include safe installation, scan limits, artifact handling, and failure criteria.

output_examples.input: Authorized directory enumeration for a staging web app.
output: A scoped scan plan with allowed host, wordlist, match codes, filters, and rate limits.
A validation checklist for confirming discovered directories and excluding false positives.

output_examples.input: Parameter fuzzing for approved API endpoints.
output: A testing sequence for parameter names, values, request methods, and response comparison.
A reporting outline that separates anomalies, confirmed findings, and follow-up checks.

output_examples.input: CI DAST gate for a staging environment.
output: A pipeline plan with controlled installation, bounded scan scope, saved artifacts, and review steps.
A failure policy for sensitive files, unexpected admin paths, and repeated scan errors.

best_practices: Confirm written authorization and exact target scope before running any fuzzing workflow.
Use small wordlists, low concurrency, and delays before increasing scan intensity.
Store outputs securely because discovered files can contain credentials or personal data.
anti_patterns: Do not fuzz third-party systems without explicit permission.
Do not run password fuzzing against production users or shared identity systems.
Do not pipe remote installer scripts into a shell without pinning and verification.

faq.question: What does this skill help me do?
faq.answer: It helps plan authorized ffuf DAST workflows for content discovery, parameter fuzzing, and virtual host testing.

faq.question: Does it run ffuf by itself?
faq.answer: No. It provides guidance and command patterns. The user or agent environment must run the tool.

faq.question: Can I use it on public targets?
faq.answer: Use it only on systems where you have written authorization and defined testing scope.

faq.question: What tools are required?
faq.answer: You need ffuf, suitable wordlists, network access to the target, and a place to store scan results.

faq.question: How should I reduce scan noise?
faq.answer: Use match filters, response size filters, auto-calibration, and manual validation before reporting findings.

faq.question: Why is this skill security sensitive?
faq.answer: It guides active web fuzzing and authentication testing, which can cause harm outside authorized environments.
